articles.title: After England setback, Babar Azam set for first domestic first-class game in seven years
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) keen to see him back in action following Pakistan’s disappointing Test tour of England.Babar to represent Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against Kingsmen Academy in the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, starting September 18. His return comes after Pakistan suffered a 0-3 series whitewash in England and the PCB made sweeping changes to the touring squad and coaching staff.PCB wants Babar back in red-ball cricketBabar has not played domestic first-class cricket since 2019, when he represented Central Punjab in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. OGDCL sports head Farah Batool said the PCB had sent his name to the team for inclusion as a guest player.“Babar’s kit has been ordered and he will decide whether to play in the match from September 18 or from September 24 in the third-round game,” Batool said.Shaheen, Haris among centrally contracted players in actionBabar is not the only centrally contracted Pakistan player featuring in domestic red-ball cricket after the England tour. Fast bowlers Shaheen Shah Afridi and Haris Rauf have also turned out for their respective teams in the President’s Trophy.Shaheen has represented KRL, claiming four wickets in an innings, while Haris picked up a five-wicket haul for PTV. Haris, who has played only one Test, against England in 2022, when he suffered an injury after bowling 13 overs, has expressed his willingness to return to Pakistan’s Test setup.“If I can be useful for Pakistan because of my pace, I would gladly play Test cricket,” he said.The fast bowler, who is primarily known for his T20 performances, had declined to play the Test series in Australia in December 2023, citing the need to manage his workload. His central contract was also suspended for a period before being restored.Babar’s captaincy under scrutiny after England whitewashBabar was reappointed Pakistan’s Test captain in July and has since overseen a 1-1 series draw against the West Indies and a 0-3 defeat to England. The PCB’s decision to make seven changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul after the second Test at Lord’s reportedly came without consulting or informing Babar.Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test came inside three days, prompting major changes ahead of the final match of the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leicestershire deducted 27 points and on brink of relegation from County Championship Division One
articles.summary: Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from County Championship Division One after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations.
articles.body:
Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from Division One of the County Championship after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations in their victory over Glamorgan in August.

The points penalty imposed by the independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) midway through their penultimate match of the season meant the Foxes have dropped to the bottom of the table.

In his interview with the Cricket Regulator before the tribunal hearing, Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin said there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

They included an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" taking place at Uptonsteel Grace Road four days before the start of the match, while Lewin also referenced the exceptionally hot weather in the build-up as another possible reason for the pitch being dry.

The pitch was rated as "poor" in the match referee's report.

Leicestershire's punishment consists of the loss of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan, an extra eight-point penalty and a £5,000 fine. A further eight-point deduction has been suspended for a year.

They can appeal the sanction within 10 working days.

In a statement, , external the club said it "notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision" and was "reviewing its position and considering all available options".

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

Just above the relegation places, the survival chances of both Glamorgan and Essex have been increased by Leicestershire's loss of points.

The Foxes' battle to avoid the drop in their first season back in Division One after a 22-year exile had been boosted by the 42-run win over Glamorgan three weeks earlier.

Before that, they had won just one match on their top-flight return after winning promotion as Division Two title winners last season.

When Leicestershire beat Glamorgan on 23 August it was immediately clear they would be in for an anxious wait to discover if the way the pitch played would have consequences.

The match officials, led by referee Ian Ramage, asked for the ECB's pitch and grounds advisor Andy Mackay to carry out an inspection after the game concluded.

After the match, Glamorgan head coach Richard Dawson said conditions were "tough" for batters.

Leicestershire head coach Alfonso Thomas added the surface had been prepared in the same way as the pitch used against Yorkshire - a game the Foxes won by an innings and 39 runs in June - although he acknowledged it was "a bit drier than what we wanted" for the match against Glamorgan.

The starting point for punishment for a pitch rated as "poor" is a 16-point deduction and this was reduced to eight points at the tribunal because of several mitigating factors.

Among them were Leicestershire's "early admission that the pitch was substandard" and this being the "first rating of below average, poor or unfit" in the previous 24 months.

A section of the judgement read: "The tribunal also takes into account Leicestershire's full co-operation with the Cricket Regulator's investigation, the fact that there was no intention to deliberately create a pitch with uneven bounce and the extreme weather conditions which do amount to some mitigation. This was not a case of cheating."

Analysis: Foxes 'gutted' about points deduction

I doubt I am being controversial by saying the pitch against Glamorgan did not play as expected. There was uneven bounce from early in the match and players were regularly getting hit on the hands.

They went for a "mullet" - shorter grass at the ends of the pitch and longer in the middle - which they have tried this week against Hampshire, to little effect, and the match before the game in question, against Yorkshire, and there was no extreme movement or bounce.

The same could not be said for this wicket.

Leicestershire felt we had a good game, which went for four days and included two scores of 90 or more. With low scores around the country that week, they did not think this pitch warranted further punishment.

The Foxes are gutted about this. They had worked so hard to work themselves back into a survival battle, only for this to ruin their chances of staying up after a 23-year wait. They need to beat Hampshire now, then title-chasing Warwickshire, and hope results elsewhere go their way. That is unlikely.

They would argue a 27-point deduction is severe and would also question whether pitches that lead to high-scoring bore draws deserve similar treatment, as well as other low-scoring pitches. However, the fact remains the club knew the rules before deciding on this pitch and it has cost them.

articles.title: County Championship: Warwickshire seal two-day win over Essex to boost title hopes as Sam Hain stars
articles.summary: Wednesday's County Championship cricket sees Warwickshire boost title hopes with two-day win vs Essex; Somerset still in title mix; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 6pm on Thursday (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
Sam Hain's unbeaten 88 helped the Bears to a first-innings lead of 57 and then Manav Suthar's five for 75 saw Essex bowled out for 189 in their second innings.

Zen Malik's 51 and an unbeaten 22 from Hain saw the visitors ease to their target of 133 for the loss of two wickets.

Somerset also remain in the hunt for the title after putting themselves in a strong position against Yorkshire .

Talismanic all-rounder Craig Overton top-scored with 64 off 111 balls as Division One leaders Somerset recovered from 86 for eight to 201 all out in reply to Yorkshire's first-innings 212 all out.

After falling as one of eight wickets for Yorkshire's excellent new-ball quick Ben Cliff, he then struck twice with the new ball himself as the hosts advanced their second innings to 128 for six and a lead of 139.

Sussex have the advantage at Hove as they ended the day on 308 for six in reply to Nottinghamshire's 240.

Tom Clarke hit 89 and Charlie Tear (50) and Tom Price (56 not out) scored half-centuries to put the hosts in charge.

A brilliant unbeaten 124 from opener Nick Gubbins put Hampshire in total control against Leicestershire . Gubbins hit 15 fours in his 224-ball knock as Hants piled up 255 for three in their second innings, a lead of 225.

Asa Tribe's magnificent 142 not out steered Glamorgan into an even better position against Surrey in their second innings. Tribe's brilliant century led his county to 339 for five in their second innings, a whopping 356 ahead.

In Division Two, Kent look set to keep their promotion hopes alive as closed day two on 84 for two in their chase of 140 against Lancashire .

The hosts took their first-innings total to 214 and a lead of 53 as Zak Crawley made 84 before Matt Milnes, Khaled Ahmed and Keith Dudgeon all took three wickets to help bowl Lancashire out for 192 in their second innings.

They slipped to 22 for two in their chase but Sam Northeast (23) and Tawanda Muyeye (37) put them on the verge of victory.

An unbeaten 87 by Adam Hose and Brett D'Oliveira's 82 helped Worcestershire fight back against Durham . Responding to Durham's 465 all out, the visitors posted 270 for five at the end of day two.

Northamptonshire trail Derbyshire by 62 runs after being bowled out for 310 while Middlesex will aim to build a big lead against Gloucestershire , currently 47 ahead with 10 second-innings wickets intact.
